claims.text: The unspecified high-performance alloy is predisposed to hot cracking during fusion processing.
Friction stir processing can be used as a solid-state repair technique on the damaged region.
Friction stir processing imposes severe plastic deformation and dynamic recrystallization.
Friction stir processing will produce a refined, recrystallized microstructure in the repair zone.
The friction-stir-processed repair zone will have reduced residual stresses.
Friction stir processing will eliminate hot-crack-susceptible features from the repair zone.
The fine-grained microstructure created by friction stir processing minimizes hot cracking.
The fine-grained microstructure created by friction stir processing minimizes residual stresses relative to fusion welding.
Traditional fusion-welded repairs are prone to residual-stress accumulation.
Hot cracking and residual-stress accumulation in a fusion-welded repair reduce mechanical performance under aggressive operating conditions.
The friction-stir-processed repair will have greater hot-cracking resistance than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The friction-stir-processed repair will have lower residual stress than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The friction-stir-processed repair will have greater fatigue resistance than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The friction-stir-processed repair will have greater tensile strength than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The proposed repair can withstand elevated temperature, cyclic mechanical loading, and potentially corrosive service conditions.
